quiz_map.support: A sanctioned assistant puts sensitive data into an answer for a person who should not see it
Both work in Microsoft Edge, and in Google Chrome and Mozilla Firefox when the Microsoft Purview extension is installed.
Mode 4 is block, so the action was stopped on the device.
PastedToBrowser records content pasted into a web page under a paste rule.
requestsize is the upload: bytes sent from the client to the server.
The DLP row names a domain, not an account.
A false positive is a match on content that is not what the rule exists to protect.
The SOC cannot verify deletion on a consumer service, so the key is treated as exposed and rotated.
A sanctioned assistant shows sensitive data to the wrong reader
Only mode 4 stops the action on the device.
Use UniqueCount to estimate how many people are affected, because one identifier repeated on many rows inflates Count.
TargetDomain names the website that received the content, which the audit record's documented endpoint fields do not.
A filled Justification means the user was warned and chose to continue.
The gateway inspects content only when ssldecrypted is Yes.
Bytes sent from the client to the server, the upload
It records the user who authenticated to the gateway, never the account signed in on the AI site.
A false positive is a match on content that is not what the rule exists to protect.
The endpoint record gives the sensitive information type and the unique count.
Deleting the conversation helps, but on a personal account the SOC cannot verify it.
Work through the worksheet in this order, because each answer feeds the next.
Pull every row for the same user and destination in the session and add up only the rows that went through.

unverified.item: Exact label of Zscaler's URL category for generative AI (raw value 'Generative AI and ML Applications')
unverified.why: Zscaler help-center pages (URL categories, release summary, NSS web log format) returned empty content (JavaScript-rendered). The 2023 Zscaler blog names the category 'AI and ML Applications'; the white paper speaks of 'Generative AI and ML applications' and of separate Generative and General AI categories.
unverified.handled: kept as a raw value only, matching the platform's existing Zscaler schema doc; never asked about or stated as a fact in teaching text

unverified.why: The Splunk guide gives the template keys but its populated example is an image; the Elastic sample shows event.action 'allowed', policy reason 'Blocked', ssl_decrypted 'Yes', dictionary 'Credit Cards'.
unverified.handled: used as raw values; the reading says 'Allowed or Blocked'. The reason field and file type labels were left out of raw because their strings could not be confirmed

unverified.why: Taken from the variable names behind the keys in the Splunk guide (reqsize, respsize, totalsize); the Zscaler definitions table did not load.
unverified.handled: stated as request bytes (client to server), response bytes and total; no finer claim (for example whether headers are included) is made as fact

unverified.item: A newer Zscaler feed template carries a prompt field
unverified.why: Seen as key prompt_req in the Elastic integration README, not in Zscaler's own documentation.
unverified.handled: softened to 'A newer feed template also carries a prompt field' with the advice to ask whether it is deployed

unverified.item: Whether EnforcementMode 3 ('warn and bypass') means the user actively bypassed the warning
unverified.why: The schema gives only the phrase 'warn and bypass'.
unverified.handled: content quotes the documented phrase and says the content 'may well have left'; confirmation is taught as coming from the Activity explorer row and the gateway

unverified.item: Literal value of Rules.RuleMode inside a record ('Enforce')
unverified.why: The schema describes the modes as Enforce, Audit with Notify, or Audit only without showing a sample record.
unverified.handled: used 'Enforce' as the raw value; no question depends on the literal string

unverified.item: Value formats in Activity explorer export rows (Application 'chrome.exe' / 'msedge.exe', Happened timestamp shape, FileSize in bytes, Justification holding the option text)
unverified.why: The cmdlet page documents column names, Activity and Workload values and that times are UTC, but shows no sample row.
unverified.handled: values are illustrative and labelled so in the lesson's example; questions rely on column meaning only. The EnforcementMode column was left out of the room's Activity explorer row because its value format there is not documented

unverified.item: The 'purview.' and 'data.office365.' key prefixes and the flattening of PolicyDetails / Rules / SensitiveInformation arrays into dotted keys
unverified.why: These are the platform's registry representation, not Microsoft field names; in the real record PolicyDetails, Rules and SensitiveInformation are collections.
unverified.handled: kept to satisfy the log-field registry; the lesson's codeExample shows the native nested JSON

unverified.item: Where an endpoint record carries the destination website and the user's override
unverified.why: The Management Activity API schema's EndpointMetadata lists only SensitiveInformation, EnforcementMode, FileExtension, FileType and DeviceName; fields such as a target domain are not documented there. ExceptionInfo.Justification is documented, but the page says override information is included for Exchange and I could not confirm it is populated for endpoint events.
unverified.handled: destination and justification are taught from the Activity explorer export columns (TargetDomain, Justification), which are documented; they were left out of the audit-record raw block

unverified.why: The fetched dist/ATLAS.yaml reports version 5.6.0 and carries a notice that this distribution file is no longer updated; the newer data layout in the repository was not read.
unverified.handled: only AML.T0057 and AML.T0024 are cited, with the name and tactic read from that file; integrate mode should re-check them against the current ATLAS release

unverified.item: Retention or purge period for deleted conversations on individual (consumer) ChatGPT accounts
unverified.why: The 30 day figure read on OpenAI's enterprise privacy page applies to ChatGPT Enterprise, Edu and Healthcare.
unverified.handled: left out; the content says deletion on a personal account cannot be verified, and a quiz distractor that promises a thirty day purge is marked wrong for that reason

unverified.item: Size reasoning in lesson section 5 (a request slightly larger than the file is consistent with the file going up in one piece)
unverified.why: General HTTP reasoning by the author, not read in a source.
